Text:
# Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Transrectal Ultrasound Prostate Biopsy Procedures The recommendations for prophylaxis for transrectal ultrasound guided prostate biopsy procedures have been updated based on emergence of resistant E-coli bacteria strains.

---

References:

- Becopoulos T et al  J Chemother 1990 2:244-246
- Charalabopoolos et al Chemotherapy 2003 49:269-279
- Nam R et al J Urol 2010 183:963-969
Therapy:
## Preferred:

## Outpatient Prescriptions for Mailing:

Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once ($) R,DI < AND >

Cefuroxime 1000 mg po once ($) [M], BOTH 2 to 3 hours before scheduled prostate biopsy.

## Outpatient Prescriptions for Window Pick-up:

Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once ($) R,DI < AND >

Cefuroxime 1000 mg po once ($) [M], BOTH 2 to 3 hours before scheduled prostate biopsy.

## Alternative for patients who have not taken the oral medications:

## Administer in clinic on the day of procedure.

## Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once ($) [R,DI] < AND > Ceftriaxone 250 mg

Intramuscularly once ($) [M] BOTH given 1 hour before the procedure.

## Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV once ($) [R,DI] < AND > Ceftriaxone 250 mg

Intramuscularly once ($) [M] BOTH given 1 hour before the procedure.

## Ceftriaxone IM preparation: Using sterile technique, inject 0.9 ml of 1% lidocaine into 250 mg ceftriaxone powder vial. Shake vial thoroughly to dissolve powder. Withdraw entire contents of vial into syringe and inject Intramuscularly.
As with all intramuscular preparations, ceftriaxone should be injected deep into the body of a large muscle. Pull back on plunger before injection to to test whether needle has inadvertently entered a blood vessel.
